Nikhilesh Dutta, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners.

parties:
Anuj Choudhury & others ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Sailendra Kishore Chowdhury and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mahfuzur Rahman J: This Rule under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against an order passed by District Judge, Noakhali on 25-3-95 in Probate Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 1993 rejecting an application refusing to summon transferees to produce documents. 

 2. The short facts for the purpose of disposal of the Rule are that, the opposite party No. 1 being petitioner instituted Probate Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 1993 under section 290 of the Succession Act, 1925 for granting him letters of Administration. The present petitioner Nos. 1, 2, 3-5 being next of kin appeared in the case and contested the granting of Letters of Administration by filing two separate written objections against the opposite party No.1 challenging his competency, integrity and that the next of kins were not made parties and those who are not legal heirs are made parties. Further alleging that the previous executor Shyama Charan namely; 4th Executor who obtained the Letters of Administration in Probate Miscellaneous Case No. 20 of 1959, already distributed the properties covered by will to the legal heirs according to their proportionate share who are owning and possessing the same without any interference from any quarter and have been paying their individual taxes living separately. The present applicant cannot be an executor since he is sacked police officer for misconduct nor resides in the will property nor practises in Moakhali Court and lives at Dhaka and Chittagong. Moreover, before being an executor he went on threatening these present petitioners to oust them from their ancestral properties. As per provision of the will he being an addicted in alcohol cannot be an executor and his own uncle Ramesh Chandra Chowdhury sold out many lands by different Kabala from the will property. After his death his son Swapan Kishore also sold out land where the executor applicant himself was a witness in the sale deed. Ripon Chowdhury sold out many lands from the will property on different occasions within the knowledge of the applicant. The Will have been rendered ineffective by way of owning, possessing and selling to different persons by the legal heirs obtaining proportionate share. 

 3. The petitioner Nos. 3-6 also filed written objection denying the claim of the executor in the Probate Miscellaneous Case for Letters of Administration and challenged his competency, integrity, honesty in the above way contending that as being addicted in wine and a corrupt person cannot be an Executor against the provision of Will and that the Will property has lost its character and nature because of having been distributed to the legal heirs and being transferred to different persons by all the legal heirs made the Will ineffective and, as such, the application should be rejected. 

 4. While the case was thus proceeding petitioner Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 4 filed two separate applications praying for summoning those transferees to come with their transfer deeds before the court for ends of justice giving in details the names and addresses of the persons to whom the applicant's uncle Ramesh Chandra Chowdhury and his cousins Swapan Kishore Chowdhury and Ripan Chowdhury transferred many lands from the Will property by different registered kabalas to different persons within his knowledge and in some transfer deeds he was the attesting witness. 

 7. Mr. Nikhilesh Dutta, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing in the case for the petitioners, since the Government is not involved, submits that the learned District Judge committed an error of law in passing the impugned order rejecting the applications without assigning any reason for the same. He points out from the impugned order that by a single stroke he rejected the application stating simply all other petitions are rejected at this stage which cannot be sustained in law. He submits that every order is to be passed by the court en proper consideration and giving reasons either in allowing or rejecting. 

 "295. In any case before the District Judge in which there is contention, the proceedings shall take, as nearly as may be, the form of a regular suit, according to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in which the petitioner for probate or letters of administration, as the case may be, shall be the plaintiff, and the person who has appeared to oppose the grant shall be the defendant. 

 He submits that the proceeding before the learned District Judge is a case for granting letters of administration as per section 295 of the Succession Act and the District Judge shall proceed in the form of a regular suit, according to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and section 299 of the Succession Act provides that every order made by a District Judge by virtue of the power hereby conferred upon him shall be subject to appeal to the High Court Division and accordingly, the revision is incompetent. He submits that the petitioner ought to have preferred an appeal against the order. Mr. Habibullah frankly conceded that the impugned order rejecting the application passed by the learned District Judge is a non-speaking order but resists the Rule as not maintainable. 

 9. In reply to this Mr. Nikhilesh Dutta, the learned Advocate, referring to sections 295 and 299 of the Succession Act submits that every order means every final order and it has not specifically mentioned that the appeal shall lie against the interlocutory and the interlocutory order is very much revisable by this court on revision. In support of his contention he referred the case of T J George vs Mrs Lucy Kochuvareed, Cr reported in AIR 1963 Kerala 188. But fails to cite any decision on the point. 

 10. Heard the learned Advocates. It appears that in this case the opposite party No. 1 being petitioner instituted the instant Probate Miscellaneous Case for granting Letters of Administration. It was objected to by the present petitioners being next of kin and others. 

 11. In this Rule we are to decide only on the point of maintainability of this revision. From the reading of section 295 it appears that in a case for probate or letters of administration before the District Judge, in which there is contention, the proceedings shall take, as nearly as may be, in the form of a regular suit according to the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure. So we find this section clearly provides how the District Judge will proceed with such case, i.e., granting letters of administration, obviously according to the Civil Procedure Code. Section 299 provides that every order made by a District Judge by virtue of the powers hereby conferred upon him shall be subject to appeal to the High Court Division in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure. From the careful reading of the statute we are of the view that every order including interlocutory order passed by the District Judge is subject to appeal. Considering the legal position and on careful reading of the decisions referred by the learned Advocate of the petitioner Mr. Dutta, we find the facts and principles laid down there are quite distinguishable and not applicable in the present case. Mr. Dutta failed to show us anything or any other provision of law that interlocutory order in such cases are subject to revision.
